examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Distance-vector uses neighbour distance estimates and Bellman–Ford updates; link-state distributes topology and runs Dijkstra. OSPF is intra-domain and supports hierarchical areas; BGP handles inter-domain path policy. Count paths and routing metrics under the stated protocol, without assuming the globally shortest physical route is always selected.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A distance-vector router has neighbours with link costs 2,5 and advertised destination distances 7,1. What new destination distance does it compute?

**Answer: 6.** Candidate routes cost 2+7=9 and 5+1=6. The Bellman–Ford update takes the minimum, 6, via the second neighbour.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Distance-vector convergence can suffer count-to-infinity. Poison reverse/split horizon mitigate specific loops but do not make every topology instantly convergent.

A router’s next hop is not necessarily the destination itself.
